met-on-paper.sentence: He learned his Stoicism from a book — his tutor Rusticus handed him the *Discourses* of Epictetus, a former *slave*, and the emperor took a slave's philosophy as his own.
met-on-paper.claim: Why a book: Epictetus died around 135, in Greece, when Marcus was about fourteen and in Rome; Marcus turned to philosophy at twenty-five (146/147), about eleven years later, and came to know Epictetus through notes of his lectures lent by Rusticus (year not recorded). The Meditations were written later still, on campaign, inside the plague years and the northern war. 'From a book' is the page's; the why, and the two lives on one axis, are the maker's, every date from two sources in dates.json.
chain: hand: make.py reads dates.json, refuses to draw any date with fewer than two sources, draws the two lifelines, the bands and the axis as SVG with soft ends for uncertain dates, and rasterises the PNG at 2x through headless Chrome

met-on-paper-2.sentence: He learned his Stoicism from a book — his tutor Rusticus handed him the *Discourses* of Epictetus, a former *slave*, and the emperor took a slave's philosophy as his own.
met-on-paper-2.claim: Why it was a book: Marcus was never Epictetus's pupil. For about fourteen years (121 to c. 135) both were alive, the boy in Rome, the teacher at Nicopolis in Greece, and the boy took up a philosopher's cloak at twelve within those years; what reached Marcus of Epictetus was notes of his lectures, lent by Rusticus, in a year no source gives. 'From a book' is the page's; the why and the two lines are the maker's, every date from two sources in dates-2.json.
chain: hand: make2.py reads dates-2.json only, refuses a date with fewer than two sources or a label carrying its own digits, formats every printed number from the data, draws two lifelines and the undated path of the notes to Marcus's name, and rasterises the PNG at 2x through headless Chrome
